key_insight: MICViT improves multimodal brain MRI learning by separately modeling local and global, as well as intra- and cross-modal, context in 3D transformer attention.
clinical_relevance: Better use of multiple MRI sequences may improve brain age modeling and other neuroimaging tasks by extracting more complementary information from each modality.
method: Four attention paths: modality-specific local, modality-specific global, cross-modal local, cross-modal global
Evaluated on brain age prediction across heterogeneous datasets with multiple MRI modalities
evidence_signal: It was tested on UK Biobank (n=41,404), SOOP (n=1,062), and Cam-CAN (n=613) and consistently outperformed CNN and transformer baselines in 3D settings.
watch_item: The approach is computationally complex and may be harder to deploy or reproduce across sites with different MRI protocols and modality availability.
paper_title: Modeling Local, Global, and Cross-Modal Context in Multimodal 3D MRI
